1) The above results were reviewed by the Audit Committee and approved by the Board of Directors at the respective meetings held on Nov 14, 2026.

2) The financial results for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026 of the parent company on consolidation basis have been subjected to a "Limited Review" by the Statutory Auditors of the Company.

3) The consolidated audited financial results includes the interim financial information of three subsidiaries and one joint venture, which have not been reviewed by their auditors and are considered based on accounts certified by their respective management.

4) The financial statements of the subsidiaries namely, BGR Boilers Private Limited and BGR Turbines Company Private Limited for the year ended 31.03.2026 are audited and included in the consolidation.

5) These Consolidated Financial results have been prepared in accordance with the recognition and measurement principles laid down in the Ind AS 34 "Interim Financial Reporting" prescribed under section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013. The Interim Consolidated Financial results are prepared and presented in accordance with the significant accounting policies and methods, as adopted in the audited consolidated financial statements for the year ended 31st March 2026.

6) In respect of the NUPPL Ghatampur Balance of plant works contract, there were an additional works to be executed by the parent company beyond the original scope of the contract. The Parent company has raised a claim of Rs.162042 lakhs with customer.
Pending approval from the customer and revision/amendment of work order, the parent company has charged the cost/expenses incurred to the Statement of Profit and Loss Account. During the quarter ended 30th Sep 2026, the charged to profit and loss account is Rs.3191 lakhs and cumulative cost charged to P&L from Jul'24 to Sep'26 on account of this is Rs.44687 lakhs.

7) With respect to the NTTPS Vijayawada Balance of Plant Works contract, there were additional works executed by the parent Company beyond the original scope of the contract. The parent company has raised a claim of Rs 76980 lakhs with the customer. the claim is pending for admission by customer. The parent Company is taking up its claim through legal course.
Pending approval from the customer and revision/amendment of work order, the parent company has charged the cost/expenses incurred to the Statement of Profit and Loss Account. During the quarter ended 30th Sep 2026, the charge to profit and loss account is Rs.1789 lakhs and cumulative cost charged to P&L from Jan'26 to Sep'26 on account of this is Rs.9362 lakhs.

8) During the quarter ended 30 Sep 2026, the parent Company has received sanction letter dated 10th Sep 2026 and the master restructuring agreement with the National Asset Reconstruction Company (ARC) in respect of its outstanding debt on 05th Oct 2026.
Pursuant to the restructuring arrangement, the outstanding debt of the parent Company amounting to Rs. 423670 lakhs as at 30 June 2026 has been considered for restructuring, with October 2025 being identified as the cut-off date. Accordingly, the debt outstanding as at the cut-off date amounted to Rs.373600 lakhs, comprising sustainable debt of Rs.124500 lakhs and unsustainable debt of Rs. 249100 lakhs.
The difference between the outstanding debt as at the reporting date and the debt determined as at the cut-off date, amounting to Rs.50355 lakhs, represents the benefit arising from the debt restructuring arrangement. The said benefit has been recognised as an exceptional item during the quarter.
Further, interest expense amounting to Rs.17177 lakhs pertaining to the first quarter, which had been recognised as finance cost, has been adjusted against the aforesaid restructuring benefit as the interest has been considered only upto 30th September 2025 as per the restructuring agreement. Accordingly, the net gain arising from the debt restructuring arrangement, amounting to Rs.33,178 lakhs, has been recognised as an exceptional item in the Statement of Profit and Loss for the quarter ended 30 September 2026.

9) During the current interim reporting period, the parent Company has reassessed the recoverability of certain Trade Receivables, Contract Assets and the Other Current Assets (BG Encashment) arising from a terminated NCTPS, ETPS, TANGEDCO and TRANSTANSCO Projects in view of the Legal developments relating to the said contracts.
The underlying contract has been terminated, and the Hon'ble Madras High Court, vide its order dated 8 October 2026, has held that the arbitration mechanism under the contract cannot be invoked.
The parent company had initially assessed that the recovery of the amounts due in respect of the aforesaid trade receivables and contract assets would be pursued through the arbitration mechanism and realised pursuant to the arbitral award. However, in view of the aforesaid order of the Hon'ble Madras High Court, the arbitration mechanism is no longer available to the parent Company for pursuing such recovery. Consequently, the parent company has reassessed the recoverability of these balances and concluded that they are credit-impaired amounting to Rs.57604 lakhs.
Accordingly, considering the uncertainty surrounding the recovery of the aforesaid amounts, the parent Company has recognised an impairment allowance equivalent to 100% of the outstanding trade receivables and contract assets relating to the said contract, in accordance with the requirements of Ind AS 109 – Financial Instruments.
The parent Company will continue to monitor any further developments in the matter and reassess the recoverability of these balances in subsequent reporting periods, as appropriate.

10) The parent company has reassessed the recoverability of trade receivables and contract assets (net) recognised in respect of NTPC projects (Solapur, Meja and Lara) undertaken with the customer. Based on the assessment of the recoverability of the outstanding balances amounting to Rs.28885 lakhs including the underlying contractual obligations and the circumstances surrounding the project, the parent company has identified certain amounts as credit-impaired, as the recovery of such amounts is no longer considered reasonably certain.
Accordingly, in accordance with the requirements of Ind AS 109 – Financial Instruments, the parent company has recognised an Expected Credit Loss (ECL) allowance at Rs.27967 lakhs of the identified credit-impaired trade receivables and contract assets. The parent Company has retained trade receivable balance at Rs.918 Lakhs. The resulting impairment loss has been recognised in the Statement of Profit and Loss for the interim reporting period.
The parent company will continue to monitor the recoverability of the outstanding balances and reassess the adequacy of the ECL provision at each subsequent reporting date, based on the facts and circumstances prevailing at that time.

11) The Honourable NCLT order appointing IRP was made on 17.04.2026. The said order was stayed by Honourable NCLAT on 30.04.2026 and extended the stay till the next hearing on 16.11.2026.

12) The accounts are prepared based on going concern basis only. The Promoters have infused unsecured loan of Rs.45818 lakhs for business operation till date. Though there has been encashment of Bank Guarantees, the Parent Company is continuing to execute the contracts and are hopeful of amicable solutions.

13) The Parent Company, with the assistance of an external consultant, has undertaken a detailed review of the balances outstanding in the operational creditors' ledgers to assess the existence and extent of its present obligations in respect of such balances. Based on the outcome of this review and the exercise of significant management judgment, the Parent Company has concluded that certain amounts outstanding to operational creditors are no longer represent present obligations of the Parent Company. Accordingly, commercial debit notes aggregating to Rs. 4460.25 lakhs have been raised against the concerned vendors in accordance with the contractual provisions.

Further, the Parent Company has written back operational creditor balances amounting to Rs.3056.75 lakhs in respect of liabilities which, based on its legal assessment, have become unenforceable owing to the expiry of the limitation period prescribed under the Limitation Act, 1963. Consequently, such liabilities have been derecognised on the basis that they are no longer considered to represent present obligations requiring settlement.

14) The figures for the previous period have been regrouped/rearranged wherever necessary to conform to the current period's classification.
